story: As a shopper, I want my Aurora Storefront account to lock after too many wrong password attempts, so that nobody can guess their way into my account.
criteria:
Scenario: Lock after repeated failures
  Given a shopper with an active account
  When they enter a wrong password 5 times within 10 minutes
  Then the account is locked

Scenario: Lock duration
  Given a locked account
  When 30 minutes have not yet passed
  Then sign-in is refused even with the correct password

Scenario: The shopper is told
  Given the account has just locked
  When the lock message appears
  Then it names the 30 minute duration

Scenario: Counter resets
  Given a shopper has failed fewer than 5 times
  When they sign in successfully
  Then the failed attempt counter returns to zero

Scenario: Support unlock
  Given a locked account
  When support staff unlock it from the admin console
  Then the shopper can sign in straight away

test_cases.title: Account locks on the fifth wrong password within 10 minutes
test_cases.pre_conditions: Shopper 'dana.reed@example.com' has an active Aurora Storefront account and 0 recorded failed attempts
steps: Open the Aurora Storefront sign-in page
Enter 'dana.reed@example.com' in the email field
Enter 'WrongPass1!' in the password field and submit
Repeat the wrong password submission four more times within 10 minutes
Observe the response after the fifth submission
test_cases.expected_result: After the fifth failure the account state changes to Locked, the sign-in form is replaced by the lockout message, and no session cookie is issued
test_cases.bdd_scenario:
Given a shopper with an active account
And the account has no recorded failed attempts
When the shopper submits a wrong password 5 times within 10 minutes
Then the account is locked
And no session is created

test_cases.title: Locked account refuses the correct password for 30 minutes
steps: Open the sign-in page
Enter 'dana.reed@example.com' and the correct password 'RightPass9!'
Submit the form
test_cases.expected_result: Sign-in is refused, the lockout message is shown with the remaining time, and the audit log records a blocked attempt on a locked account
test_cases.bdd_scenario:
Given a locked account
And 30 minutes have not yet passed
When the shopper submits the correct password
Then sign-in is refused

test_cases.title: Lockout message names the 30 minute duration
test_cases.pre_conditions: Account 'dana.reed@example.com' has just reached its fifth failed attempt
steps: Trigger the fifth failed sign-in attempt
Read the message shown above the sign-in form
test_cases.expected_result: The message reads 'Your account is locked for 30 minutes.' and the duration is stated in minutes, not in a relative phrase such as 'a while'
test_cases.test_data: expected_copy=Your account is locked for 30 minutes.
test_cases.bdd_scenario:
Given the account has just locked
When the lock message appears
Then it names the 30 minute duration

test_cases.title: Successful sign-in resets the failed attempt counter
test_cases.pre_conditions: Account 'dana.reed@example.com' has 3 recorded failed attempts and is not locked
steps: Sign in with the correct password 'RightPass9!'
Sign out
Enter a wrong password twice
Check the stored failed attempt count
test_cases.expected_result: The counter is 0 immediately after the successful sign-in and 2 after the two later failures, so the account does not lock
test_cases.bdd_scenario:
Given a shopper has failed fewer than 5 times
When they sign in successfully
Then the failed attempt counter returns to zero

test_cases.title: Lockout message does not reveal whether the email is registered
test_cases.pre_conditions: The email 'nobody@example.com' has no Aurora Storefront account
steps: Submit 'nobody@example.com' with a wrong password five times
Compare the message with the one shown for a registered email
test_cases.expected_result: Both paths show the same generic message and the same response timing, so an attacker cannot tell registered emails from unregistered ones
test_cases.bdd_scenario:
Given an email with no account
When five wrong passwords are submitted
Then the response is indistinguishable from a registered email

test_cases.title: Password reset is still refused while the account is locked
steps: Open the sign-in page
Follow the 'Forgot password' link
Submit 'dana.reed@example.com'
test_cases.expected_result: The reset flow does not silently unlock the account; after setting a new password the shopper still waits out the remaining lock time
test_cases.bdd_scenario:
Given a locked account
When the shopper completes a password reset
Then the lock is still in force

test_cases.title: Four failures followed by the correct password do not lock the account
steps: Submit a wrong password four times within 10 minutes
Submit the correct password 'RightPass9!'
test_cases.expected_result: Sign-in succeeds on the fifth submission, the account is never locked, and the counter is reset to 0
test_cases.bdd_scenario:
Given a shopper with 0 failed attempts
When they fail 4 times and then succeed
Then the account is not locked

test_cases.title: Five failures spread over more than 10 minutes do not lock the account
test_cases.pre_conditions: Account 'dana.reed@example.com' has 0 recorded failed attempts and the clock can be controlled
steps: Submit a wrong password four times over 9 minutes
Advance the clock to 11 minutes after the first attempt
Submit a wrong password once more
test_cases.expected_result: The first attempt has fallen outside the 10 minute window, so only 4 attempts count and the account stays unlocked
test_cases.bdd_scenario:
Given four failures inside the window
When a fifth failure happens after the window has moved on
Then the account is not locked

test_cases.title: Sign-in works again at exactly 30 minutes after the lock
steps: Wait until the clock reads 30 minutes after the lock
Submit the correct password 'RightPass9!'
test_cases.expected_result: Sign-in succeeds at 30:00, and a check at 29:59 is still refused
test_cases.bdd_scenario:
Given an account locked 30 minutes ago
When the shopper submits the correct password
Then sign-in succeeds

test_cases.title: Failures from two browsers count towards the same account lock
test_cases.pre_conditions: Account 'dana.reed@example.com' has 0 recorded failed attempts; two browsers are open
steps: Submit three wrong passwords in browser A
Submit two wrong passwords in browser B within the same 10 minutes
Attempt to sign in from either browser
test_cases.expected_result: The counter is held per account, not per browser, so the fifth failure locks the account for both browsers
test_cases.bdd_scenario:
Given failures from two browsers
When the combined count reaches 5 within 10 minutes
Then the account is locked everywhere

test_cases.title: Lock survives closing and reopening the browser
steps: Close the browser completely
Reopen it and clear cookies
Submit the correct password 'RightPass9!'
test_cases.expected_result: The lock is stored against the account on the server, so a fresh browser is still refused and the message still names the remaining time
test_cases.bdd_scenario:
Given a locked account
When the shopper returns in a fresh browser
Then sign-in is still refused

test_cases.title: Lock message counts down to the last whole minute
steps: Open the sign-in page with 60 seconds of the lock left
Read the lockout message
Wait until 30 seconds remain and read it again
test_cases.expected_result: The message reads '1 minute' at 60 seconds and 'less than a minute' below 60 seconds; it never shows a negative or zero duration
test_cases.bdd_scenario:
Given a lock with one minute left
When the shopper reads the message
Then the remaining time is stated in whole minutes

test_cases.title: A failed sign-in does not reset the attempt counter
steps: Submit a wrong password once more
Read the stored failed attempt count
test_cases.expected_result: The counter moves to 4, never back to 0; only a successful sign-in resets it
test_cases.bdd_scenario:
Given a shopper with 3 failed attempts
When another attempt fails
Then the counter is not reset

test_cases.title: Support unlocks a locked account from the admin console
test_cases.pre_conditions: Account 'dana.reed@example.com' locked 2 minutes ago; a support user is signed in to the admin console
steps: Open the account in the admin console
Select 'Unlock account'
Ask the shopper to sign in with the correct password
test_cases.expected_result: The lock is cleared at once, the shopper signs in without waiting out the 30 minutes, and the unlock is written to the audit log with the support user's name
test_cases.bdd_scenario:
Given a locked account
When support unlocks it from the admin console
Then the shopper can sign in straight away

test_cases.title: A shopper without support rights cannot unlock an account
test_cases.pre_conditions: Account 'dana.reed@example.com' is locked; a signed-in shopper has no admin role
steps: Call the unlock endpoint directly as the ordinary shopper
Check the account state
test_cases.expected_result: The request is refused with an authorisation error, the account stays locked, and the refused attempt is logged
test_cases.bdd_scenario:
Given a shopper with no admin role
When they call the unlock endpoint
Then the request is refused and the lock remains

test_cases.title: Unlocking one second before the lock expires still works
test_cases.pre_conditions: Account 'dana.reed@example.com' locked 29 minutes and 59 seconds ago
steps: Unlock the account from the admin console at 29:59
Sign in immediately with the correct password
test_cases.expected_result: The unlock is accepted at 29:59 and sign-in succeeds without waiting for the final second; the audit log records one unlock, not two
test_cases.bdd_scenario:
Given a lock with one second left
When support unlocks the account
Then sign-in succeeds immediately

summary.automation_coverage_potential: 55% -- the lock and counter rules are straightforward to automate; the timing and multi-browser cases need clock control and parallel sessions.
coverage_gaps: Support staff unlocking an account early from the admin console is not covered.
No case checks the audit trail an unlock writes.
recommendations: Add a case for the support unlock path before release.
Give the test environment a controllable clock so the timing cases can run unattended.
Run the enumeration case on every release; it guards a security promise.
